title: Demand side: who would buy escort
description: The buyer is not the ship. It is one of four parties in the ownership stack, and which one pays depends on the charter. This dataset holds the demand side in two tiers: companies with a vessel actually attacked, and the operator population in the segments that get attacked most. Roles and definitions come from ownership-model.json.

buying_roles.note: Taken from ownership-model.json, where buys_security is recorded per role. Four of the eight roles buy security.

gaps: Honour 25 remains the one attacked vessel researched with no owner, manager or charterer found anywhere, despite being under confirmed naval seizure.
No contact route is recorded for any company here. The resolution path in ownership-model.json ends at the ISM manager; that step has not been run.
Fleet sizes for the dry bulk operators come from a secondary listicle, not from a registry. They should be checked against Equasis or Clarksons before use.
Charterers are almost absent. On time and voyage charters the charterer usually bears the war risk premium, which makes them a buyer, but this library names only Cargill.
No company here has been confirmed to currently buy any form of armed or escort protection.
Tanker fleet counts mix owned and managed vessels; several sources do not say which. Not comparable across companies without checking each.
Headquarters country is missing for Hafnia, Bahri and Stolt Tankers in the fetched sources.
4 of 10 exposed companies have no verifiable official website: Allseas Marine, Evalend Shipping, Third January Maritime Ltd, SR Shipping. Three of those four are Greek managers.
Lila Norfolk's chain comes from a vessel-tracking aggregator (MagicPort), not primary shipping press. Confidence is medium, not high, pending Equasis.
exposed_note: One row per company named in a party role on a vessel that was attacked. Compiled 2026-09-03 from contemporaneous reporting. Where a source named only the flag or the vessel type, no company is recorded rather than a guess. Brokers are excluded: they are not a party that buys security.

ship_managers.title: Third-party technical managers
ship_managers.why_this_matters: Technical managers buy security under this library's own ownership model. Unlike owners, they are concentrated: five firms account for roughly 3,100 vessels under management between them. Counts are total managed fleet across all vessel types, not tanker-only or bulk-only.
